did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens by introducing Elkanah, who came from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. His ancestry is given through his forefathers: Jeroham, Elihu, Tohu, and Zuph.
Did you know? Every year, Elkanah went up to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts. Hophni and Phinehas, Eli’s sons, served there as priests of the LORD.
Did you know? Although Hannah had no children, Elkanah loved her and gave her a special portion at the sacrificial meal. The text notes that the LORD had closed her womb.
Did you know? Elkanah tried to comfort Hannah by asking whether he was not better to her than ten sons, but his words also highlight the depth of her pain and her longing for a child.

Did you know? Hannah vowed that if she were given a son, she would dedicate him to the LORD for all the days of his life, and no razor would ever touch his head. In this way, she connected her request with dedicating the child to the LORD’s service.
Did you know? Hannah prayed silently; only her lips moved. Eli the priest saw her, but he did not understand her situation and thought she was drunk.
Did you know? Hannah explained to Eli that she was not drunk, but a deeply troubled woman pouring out her soul before the LORD. She described her prayer as an expression of her profound sorrow.
Did you know? After Eli blessed her, Hannah went on her way, ate, and was no longer sad. The chapter describes a change in her condition even before it became clear that her prayer had been answered.
Did you know? After Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, she named him Samuel, saying, “I asked him of the LORD.” His name was therefore connected with her request to the LORD.
Did you know? After Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to Shiloh with offerings: three bulls, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, to present him before the LORD.
Did you know? Hannah explained to Eli that Samuel was the child for whom she had prayed and whom she had received from the LORD. She declared that she was lending him to the LORD for all his days.
